product.label: VyrnForge Reference
product.purpose: One reader-facing product for VyrnForge guidance, generated reference facts, executable examples, and versioned framework context across Docs and Playground.
product.hostPolicy: The React host is an implementation detail. Native HTML, React, Angular, and Vue remain equal reader contexts and no React-only presentation contract may become canonical VyrnForge semantics.

native-html.label: Native HTML
native-html.guidance: Use registered VyrnForge Custom Elements directly with shared tokens, DOM events, slots, methods, and form contracts.

react.label: React
react.guidance: Use the React renderer while keeping behavior, tokens, accessibility, and public contracts aligned with the shared VyrnForge foundation.

angular.label: Angular
angular.guidance: Use the verified Angular consumer and adapter contracts over the shared VyrnForge element surface; do not invent framework-only behavior.

vue.label: Vue
vue.guidance: Use the verified Vue consumer and model-adapter contracts over the shared VyrnForge element surface; keep events and state semantics portable.

docs.label: Docs
docs.role: curated guidance and generated reference presentation

playground.label: Playground
playground.role: executable examples, interaction exploration, and reference presentation

guides.policy: Human guidance owns explanation and recommendations but must link to canonical structured facts instead of repeating API truth.

components.policy: Public API facts, framework parity, accessibility contracts, and component catalog facts are generated from canonical metadata and contracts; presentation may add curated guidance without restating those facts manually.

packages.policy: Package identity, relationships, release lines, and public entrypoint facts come from package metadata, manifests, and verified public entrypoints rather than application registries.

tokens.policy: Token reference data is derived from shared VyrnForge token contracts and runtime CSS custom properties; reference surfaces do not own theme or token values.

patterns.policy: Pattern identity and relationships come from canonical pattern metadata while longer workflow guidance remains curated documentation.

examples.policy: Executable example identity and framework evidence are registry-backed. Surface-specific example code may be authored, but equivalent semantic examples use shared identities and verification contracts.

accessibility.policy: Accessibility behavior and keyboard contracts come from shared component contracts and evidence; explanatory guidance may be curated without redefining framework-specific behavior.

search.policy: Search indexes generated reference records and curated text. It never becomes an independent source for API, package, token, framework, or release facts.

routing.policy: Route IDs are shared semantic identities. Current hand-maintained registries remain transitional runtime inputs until generated replacements are verified; they must not own component, package, token, framework, version, or API facts.

deployment.policy: Preview and production artifacts preserve Docs and Playground as one deployable Reference product while retaining commit and CI lineage.
